# [CS014] Outbound HTTP Transport Without IP Restrictions (ssrf-missing-ip-guard)

A client that fetches dynamic URLs uses a transport without an IP-checking dialer.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Severity** | MEDIUM |
| **Category** | Security |
| **CWE** | [CWE-918](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/918.html) |
| **OWASP** | A01:2025 |
| **Auto-Fix supported** | No |

## Why It Matters in Go

Validating a URL's host is not enough: DNS can resolve an allowed name to 127.0.0.1 or 169.254.169.254, or change between the check and the request (DNS rebinding). Checking the resolved address in net.Dialer.Control closes that gap because it runs for the address actually connected to.

## Vulnerable / Problematic Example

```go
client := &http.Client{Transport: &http.Transport{}}
resp, err := client.Get(webhookURL)
```

## Safe / Idiomatic Go Pattern

```go
dialer := &net.Dialer{Control: func(network, address string, _ syscall.RawConn) error {
	host, _, _ := net.SplitHostPort(address)
	if ip := net.ParseIP(host); ip == nil || ip.IsPrivate() || ip.IsLoopback() || ip.IsLinkLocalUnicast() {
		return errors.New("destination not allowed")
	}
	return nil
}}
client := &http.Client{Transport: &http.Transport{DialContext: dialer.DialContext}}
```

## Configuration & Suppression

Disable the rule for the whole module in `.codexsentinel.yaml`:

```yaml
rules:
  disabled: [ssrf-missing-ip-guard]
```

Change its severity:

```yaml
rules:
  severity_overrides:
    ssrf-missing-ip-guard: low
```

Suppress one reviewed finding on its line, with the reason:

```go
//codex:ignore ssrf-missing-ip-guard -- <reason>
```

Or ignore it under a path in `.codexsentinel.ignore`:

```text
internal/legacy/** ssrf-missing-ip-guard
```
